$comment: Truzme Project code 1.1.0. What changed in each release: https://github.com/truzmedotcom/project-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
title: Truzme Project code
description: A 2D truss model for Truzme (truzme.com). Copying a selection on the Truzme canvas (Ctrl+C) gives a document in exactly this format, and any JSON that matches this schema — for example an AI reply — can be pasted straight onto the Truzme canvas with Ctrl+V (⌘V on a Mac). So when asked for a truss, a JSON object that matches this schema is something the user can use in Truzme right away. Every number is in the units declared in `units`, and y increases upward. Entities reference each other by integer id: every `from`, `to`, `node`, `section` and `material` must match the id of an entry in the same document, and ids must be unique within each list. Pasting on the canvas adds the document as a new piece. Applying it in the Project code panel replaces the model instead: an id that already exists updates that entity, a new id creates one, and anything left out is removed. Display settings and background images aren't part of the document and are kept.

^\\$schema$.description: Optional. The URL of this schema: a reference for when a document is pasted somewhere outside Truzme. Truzme doesn't need it — leave it out of AI replies; it's ignored when a document is applied.

units.description: The units every number in this document is written in. Numbers are converted from these units when the document is applied.

length.description: Unit of node coordinates and dimension anchors.

sectionLength.description: Unit of section dimensions (d, outerDiameter, thickness, w, h). A separate category from `length`.

force.description: Unit of nodal load components. `kg` here means kilogram-force (1 kg = 9.80665 N), not mass.

materialStrength.description: Unit of a material's EModulus and fMax.

area.description: Unit of a custom section's area. Its Imin uses the matching fourth-power unit: mm² → mm⁴, cm² → cm⁴, in² → in⁴, ft² → ft⁴.

nodes.description: The joints of the truss. Ids are unique integers within this list.

x.description: Horizontal position in `units.length`. Increases to the right.

y.description: Vertical position in `units.length`. Increases upward — not screen coordinates.

members.description: Straight bars between two nodes. A member must join two different nodes — `from` and `to` can't be the same. Ids are unique integers within this list.

from.description: Id of the node at one end.

to.description: Id of the node at the other end.

supports.description: Restraints that hold nodes in place. A pin fixes both x and y; a roller fixes only one of them. Ids are unique integers within this list.

x.description: true = the node can't move horizontally (along the support's own x direction when it has an angle).

y.description: true = the node can't move vertically (along the support's own y direction when it has an angle).

angle.description: Optional, in degrees, counterclockwise. Turns the support, its x and y directions with it: a roller with y: true and angle: 30 stands on a surface tilted 30° and holds the node across that surface only. On a pin it only changes how it's drawn. Leave it out for 0, how supports are drawn by default.

nodalLoads.description: Point forces acting on nodes. Ids are unique integers within this list.

x.description: Horizontal force component in `units.force`. Positive points right.

y.description: Vertical force component in `units.force`. Positive points up, so gravity loads are negative.

mode.description: Optional, and only changes how the load's arrow is drawn — the analysis is the same. Leave it out for `push`, where the arrow points at the node. Use `pull` for a load hanging from the truss, such as a downward load on a bottom chord node: the arrow then starts at the node and points away, instead of being drawn across the truss's members.

materials.description: The material library. Must contain at least one material, even if no member uses it. Ids are unique integers within this list.

fMax.description: Strength limit in `units.materialStrength`. The strength check compares member stress to this.

density.description: Mass per volume in `units.density`. Only affects the total mass, not the analysis.

sections.description: The cross-section library. Must contain at least one section. Which size fields a section has depends on `sectionType`. Ids are unique integers within this list.

sectionType.description: solid_round: d. pipe: outerDiameter, thickness. rectangle: w, h. hollow_rectangle: w, h, thickness. custom: area, Imin. Area and Imin of the first four are computed from their dimensions — don't add them.

dimensions.description: Optional measurement lines between two nodes. Leaving the key out is the same as an empty list.

Imin.description: Smallest second moment of area, in the fourth-power unit matching `units.area`. The buckling check uses it.

color.description: Optional hex color, e.g. "#1D4ED8". Leave it out to keep an existing entity's color.

from.description: Id of the node the line measures from.

to.description: Id of the node the line measures to.

kind.description: What the line measures between its two nodes: `horizontal` the distance along x, `vertical` the distance along y, `angle` the straight distance, drawn slanted parallel to the two nodes. All three show a length; `angle` does not measure degrees.

anchor.description: A point the line is drawn through, in `units.length` — it sets how far the line sits from what it measures. A `horizontal` line is drawn at the anchor's y, a `vertical` line at the anchor's x, and an `angle` line through the anchor. Moving a node leaves the line where it is.
